q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM( SELECT VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE, COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS CNT FROM VIEWS GROUP BY 1,2)A WHERE CNT > 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM( SELECT VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE, COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS CNT FROM VIEWS GROUP BY 1,2)A WHERE CNT > 1
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01');
explanation: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, which means it considers the number of distinct articles viewed by each viewer on each specific date. Q2, on the other hand, groups by VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE, and then checks the count of distinct articles for each viewer on each date. The difference arises when a viewer views the same article multiple times on the same date, as Q1 will count this as a single view, while Q2 will count each view separately.
counterexample_dsp: A viewer views the same article twice on the same date. Q1 will not count this as an additional view for that viewer on that date, while Q2 will.
